messages.subject: corpling R package
parts:
coRpus linguists,

In an effort to learn how to create R packages (following http://r-pkgs.had.co.nz/), I created a package that provides two simple tools for corpus linguistics, namely, concordances and ngram frequency lists. The package is on Github:

install.packages("devtools") # if need be
library("devtools")
install_github("ekbrown/corpling")
library("corpling")

If you don't have the dependencies, it make take a bit for the package to download.

There are three function (currently):

# loads .txt files into a list, each file as an element of the list
load_txt()
?load_txt

# produces a concordance
concord()
?concord

# produces an ngram frequency list, whether single words, bigram, trigrams, etc.
ngram_freq()
?ngram_freq

Give it a try, if you'd like, and let me know what you think, ways how to improve, etc. I may or may not ever submit it to CRAN, as Github is just was easy with the devtools package, but I figured I'd share it with this list.

Earl

I have to confess that, as a complete novice to package development, I don't know why Stefan and John are having problems with installing and getting my package to work. Last night, I installed RRO 3.2.2 and tried devtools::install_github on my mac and on my wife's mac, and I was able to successfully install my package from github and the functions worked correctly. I also successfully installed my package on my home computer, running Linux Mint 17.2, using R 3.2.3.

The only suggestion I have to offer is what anyone would offer: to update your software, starting with the dependencies:

install.packages(c("devtools", "dplyr", "stringr"))

and possibly/probably R itself (if you don't already have the most recent release: R 3.2.3 or RRO 3.2.2, with MRO 3.2.3 to be released on Jan 19th).

These threads may or may not be helpful to those using RRO:

https://github.com/RevolutionAnalytics/RRO/issues/37

https://github.com/hadley/devtools/issues/406

https://github.com/hadley/devtools/issues/647


I hope this package can be useful to coRpus linguists, so please let me know if you're still unable to install and use it, and I'll spend some time investigating the situation more.

messages.author: 8dafe35eb614235f
messages.subject: Re: [CorpLing with R] Re: corpling R package
parts:
Bob,

No way currently to specify the exact number of words with concord(). However, using a combination of \\w+ and \\W+ on PRE_CONTEXT and POST_CONTEXT, with the appropriate edge line anchor ("^" or "$") would be a workaround. See QCLWR p. 81, 84.

ngram_freq(..., num_wd = 1) gives you a frequency list of single words, num_wd = 2 gives you a frequency list of bigrams, num_wd = 3 trigrams, etc. Theoretically, you could keep going as high as you want, or until num_wd is larger than the number of words in the largest element, at which point the function throws an error.

Currently, no function gives you collocations, although that is on my to-do list. See QCLWR section 4.3, staring on p. 149.

I'm glad that you got the package installed correctly.
